chunks: And it is narrated from a camel driver from whom camels were hired, and oil was sent with him to a land. He claimed that some of the oil skins had torn and the oil had spilled. He said:
If he wishes, he may take the oil.

And he said: It was torn, but he is not to be believed except with just evidence. And whichever man hires an animal, and a wolf attacks it and splits its eye so it dies, then he is liable for it unless he is a just Muslim.

key_terms.زِقَاقِ: skins or containers used for holding oil
key_terms.عَدْلًا: just and trustworthy in legal standing

ai.seo_question: When is a hired carrier or renter liable for lost or damaged property in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability in hired transport and rented animals. A mere claim of accidental loss is not accepted without just proof, and the renter is held liable unless he is established as a trustworthy and just Muslim.
